subject: BLUEPRINT VERDICT (grok): CRPS 0.01 is 0.022 SE at n=150, Shin already correct in our tests, n=70 Jackknife+ is sample destruction
body:
# BLUEPRINT VERDICT (grok)

Independent review of "Architectural Blueprint for a Calibrated, Tracking-Decoupled
Sports Probability Engine." Filed 2026-09-18. I read opus's verdict, Shin
measurement, and citation check after poll (could not unread). Everything below
was re-derived against the repo and against primary sources. Where I agree I
say so. Where they stopped at the inversion I measured the power. A document
that agrees with us is not a spec.

---

## A. The agreement trap. Two of our hunches are now written as requirements.

1. **"Anticipating a baseline market data violation rate well above five percent."**
   That is opus's pre-registered guess, quoted back as an anticipated baseline.
   I did not measure it. Nobody has. If I cite 5% after this sentence I have
   laundered a hunch. Rung 1 work is to LOG the rate, not to encode 5% as a
   threshold. Same for the "19% of spatial frames" figure, still unsourced from
   the first paper.

2. **SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError, fail-closed CQR, Venn-Abers, density-not-points,
   Route C (non-commercial tracking for offline validation only).** These are
   our verdicts written back to us. Correct, and already partly in tree. The
   danger is treating the paper as a build list for files we already have.

3. **"Decoupled" is the right concession on tracking.** Rights still block a
   live 10Hz feed. nflverse + public aggregates is the legal plane. That is
   not a finding, it is the premise. The rest of the paper has to deliver
   predictive power from that plane. It mostly relocates ambition into
   vocabulary (Knightian, curvature tensor, state-transition cost, ESOE analog).

---

## B. Repo claims. The paper describes our code, then tells us to rebuild it.

Checked, not admired.

| Paper says | Repo fact |
|---|---|
| Strip CQR quantile clamping | **Done in `apps/web/lib/calibration/cqr.ts`.** `conformalQuantile` returns +Infinity when rank > n-1. Test: `cqr-refuses-small-sample.test.ts` n=5 α=0.1. **NOT done** in `packages/prediction-engine/src/conformal-intervals.ts:64-74`, which still `Math.min(n-1, rank-1)` and returns 0 on empty. Two copies, one still fake-tight. That is my domain. |
| Deploy Jackknife+ for n≈70 | We have `jackknifeStandardError` (influence-function SE). We do **not** have Jackknife+ conformal intervals. Real gap. Wrong sample (see C.3). |
| Deploy Generalized Venn-Abers, dual PAVA, Δp>0.20 | **EXISTS.** `calibration/ivap.ts`, `cvap.ts`, `edge-lab/selective-gate.ts`. Not on the mint path. Empty calibration returns `{p0:0.5,p1:0.5,width:0}` (`ivap.ts:58-60`). Width 0 would PASS a Δp>0.20 no-bet gate. Fake tightness in the file the paper wants us to "build". |
| ACI | **EXISTS.** `conformal-intervals.ts:96` `alpha + learningRate * (targetError - miss)`, clamped to [0.02, 0.5]. Direction of the step is correct (miss → smaller α → wider). The clamp on α is another clamp. |
| Shin de-vig as THE method | **EXISTS**, and our header already has the direction the paper got backwards. `edge-lab/devig.ts:13-22`: "pulls probability mass OFF longshots and onto favourites relative to the proportional split." Side-by-side with proportional. Receipts use proportional (`AGENTS.md:1066`). Switching basis restarts the eligibility streak (`AGENTS.md:857, 1207`). Founder-only. |
| Reject Hawkes, use B-spline+RTS | Hawkes **exists** (`hawkes-steam.ts`), unused as a capital gate, honest about thin windows. No B-spline, no RTS, no Kalman in tree. |
| E-process vs Shin-devigged market, unlock when martingale breaches a boundary | `forecast-skill-eprocess.ts:30-35` is our likelihood OVER the market's. The paper does not write the ratio. The first paper wrote it upside down. Underspecified here, inverted there. Do not implement from the paper. |
| Gaussian closed-form CRPS | Kernel **types** `CrpsDiscreteFn` / `CrpsEmpiricalFn` in `edge-lab/kernel/contract.ts:208-226`. **No implementation** (no `crpsDiscrete`, no Gaussian closed form). Discrete is the right object for integer scores. Gaussian is the approximation. |
| Market logit as fixed offset | Paper never mentions it. Charter #1 remaining hole in the trainer. `logistic.ts` already accepts `offset` with coefficient pinned at 1 (`e1c5334`). Callers still mostly omit it. |
| Physical-plausibility / non-finite clocks | `asof-guard.ts` throws `SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError` on non-finite clocks (`e1c5334`). Do not rebuild. |
| Trainers refuse leaked trueProb | Gate exists (`readTrainableTrueProb`). **No trainer calls it.** `ranking-prob.ts:62-63` is fail-OPEN: it nulls only `post_settlement_backfill`, so untagged historical rows (no basis) still rank. That is the half that bites, and the paper does not know it exists. |

The paper is not a missing-file list. It is a description of machinery we have,
plus inverted gates, plus one real unbuilt object (Jackknife+), plus a density
pipeline we have typed and not run.

---

## C. Math audit. Load-bearing defects, with numbers.

### 1. The CRPS gate is inverted AND statistically empty.

Paper, CRPS section, verbatim: "measurable CRPS improvement of **less than
0.01** on a minimum sample of 150 settled spreads before advancing to live
execution."

Rung 2, verbatim: "must demonstrably **beat** the widened point-estimate CRPS
on 150+ settled spreads."

Those are opposites. I agree with opus on the inversion. Then I computed the
power, which the inversion debate hid.

Closed-form Gaussian CRPS (Gneiting & Raftery 2007):
`CRPS(N(μ,σ²), y) = σ { z(2Φ(z)−1) + 2φ(z) − 1/√π }`, `z=(y−μ)/σ`.
Calibrated expectation: `σ/√π`.

NFL score-margin σ ≈ 14 points (historical ballpark, not our measurement):
- E[CRPS] = 7.90
- "improvement of 0.01" = **0.13% relative**
- Monte Carlo: mean 7.84, sd 5.56
- SE of the mean at n=150: **0.454**
- 0.01 is **0.022 standard errors**
- n required to detect a 0.01 delta at 95%: **≈ 1.2 million**

The 0.01 line is not a kill line. It is a number that cannot fire. Even if
we reverse the inequality to "at least 0.01", it auto-passes any noise.

Pre-registered replacement, before any density model ships:

> Discrete CRPS (integer margin support), fixture-grouped, vs the widened
> Gaussian baseline with σ frozen from **prior seasons only**.
> Kill: mean CRPS_model is not lower than CRPS_baseline − 0.5 at n ≥ 272
> (one NFL regular season of games), or CRPSS = 1 − CRPS_m/CRPS_b ≤ 0.
> Direction: lower CRPS is better. 0.5 points is ~6% of the 7.9 baseline,
> about 1.1 SE at n=272 unpaired, tighter if paired. 0.01 is forbidden.

NFL scores are integers. Common margins (3, 7) are point masses. A Gaussian
closed form is an approximation that smears those. Our kernel already named
the right objects (`crpsDiscrete`, `crpsEmpirical`). Building the paper's
Gaussian as the primary score would be a step backward. Implement discrete.
Use Gaussian only as a cheap diagnostic.

Brier is CRPS of a Bernoulli. Replacing "all Brier tracking for continuous
margins" is fine. Replacing Brier for moneylines is not. The paper's table
says Brier is "incapable of evaluating continuous spreads." A spread cover
is a binary. We Brier-score it today. Keep that.

### 2. Shin direction is backwards. I re-solved the quadratic. Our code was already right.

Shin (1993) *Economic Journal* 103:1141–53 is real. The working formula
(Cain / Clarke implementation of Shin 1992/93):

`p_i = [√(z² + 4(1−z) q_i²/S) − z] / [2(1−z)]`, S = Σ q_i, q_i = 1/decimal.

I bisected z so Σ p_i = 1. Favourite is the first number.

```
market            prop_fav  shin_fav  prop−shin     z
-110 / -110         0.5000    0.5000    0.0000    0.0476
-160 / +140         0.5963    0.5994   -0.0031    0.0321
-300 / +240         0.7183    0.7279   -0.0096    0.0446
-600 / +450         0.8250    0.8377   -0.0127    0.0402
-1500 / +850        0.8991    0.9161   -0.0171    0.0467
```

Matches opus to 4 d.p. Independent confirmation, not a copy.

- Proportional **under**-weights favourites (over-weights longshots). Paper
  says overweights favourites. Backwards.
- Shin moves **away** from the midpoint. Paper says "shading … back toward
  the midpoint". Backwards. The mechanism sentence ("removes vig from the
  longshot") is half-right and contradicts the conclusion: removing more
  vig from the longshot **lowers** the longshot and **raises** the favourite.
- Symmetric book: prop = shin = 0.5, z≈0.048. A market with no
  favourite-longshot asymmetry has nothing to correct. That identity held.
- z in 0.032–0.048 is the 3–5% insider fraction the horse-racing literature
  reports. A broken solver would not land there five times.

`edge-lab/devig.ts` already states this direction and tests it
(`devig.test.ts`: "the favourite's comes in above [proportional]"). The
paper is not just wrong against the literature. It is wrong against **our
own unit tests**.

Adopting Shin as the receipt basis:

- Raises market p on heavy favourites. Our sample is dominated by heavy
  MLB favourites. Edge on those rows shrinks.
- Restarts the PROVEN eligibility streak. Founder-only.
- Shin is a **model** (assumes an insider fraction z). Whelan (2025, *The
  Manchester School*) shows nearly identical z on Tote markets that have
  **no bookmaker supply side**, so z is not cleanly "insider trading".
  Do not pay a streak reset for a structural story that is in dispute.

Keep proportional as the receipt default. Keep Shin as the side-by-side
research routine it already is. Founder decides if a basis change is worth
the streak.

### 3. Jackknife+ on n=70 H2H analogs is the charter's original sin.

Paper: NFL "full season yields only n=70 relevant head-to-head analogs",
so abandon split CQR, use Jackknife+, report 1−2α.

Jackknife+ coverage 1−2α is real (Barber, Candès, Ramdas, Tibshirani).
At α=0.10 that is 80%, not 90%. Paper reports this correctly.

Then it chooses the **smallest imaginable sample**. Charter §0: test at
the layer with the most labels. nflverse game-level margins: ~272 NFL
regular-season games per year, thousands historically. n=70 is
matchup-filtered pick-level thinking. It is how ten months disappeared.

At 80% coverage on Gaussian residuals with σ=14, half-width ≈ 1.28σ =
**±17.9 points** (full width 36). A 3-point spread does not live inside
a 36-point interval. Valid, and too wide to size a bet. Reporting 1−2α
honestly does not make the interval useful.

Worse: the paper then stacks ACI on top. Jackknife+'s 1−2α guarantee is
for a **fixed** α under exchangeability. ACI exists because sports
**violate** exchangeability. You cannot adapt α online and keep the
finite-sample 1−2α claim. That is fake tightness with extra steps — the
same class of error as clamping the conformal rank.

And it recommends Venn-Abers for binaries, which **requires a calibration
set**, after rejecting split CQR because burning half of n=70 is
"devastating". Internal contradiction in the conformal stack.

If we ever build Jackknife+, it is on game-level margins with n in the
thousands, 1−2α printed on the interval, no ACI stacked on the same
object, and a pre-registered kill: if median interval width at 80%
exceeds 14 points (one historical σ) on the holdout, the method is a
coverage trophy and we do not bet with it.

### 4. RTS Kalman on live odds is lookahead.

Rauch–Tung–Striebel is a **forward-backward** smoother. The backward pass
uses t+1…T to "smooth" time t. For offline labelling of historical steam,
legal. For live execution "before global equilibrium is restored", it is
fitting on the future path of the line.

Live-legal tool is the **forward** Kalman filter. The paper specifies RTS.
That is a leakage hole in the steam detector, same family as
in-play-exclusion keeping a row when the clock is null.

"Parameter-free" is false. Cubic B-splines have knot placement. RTS has
process and measurement noise (Q, R). Hawkes has (μ, α, β). Trading one
parameter set for another and calling it parameter-free is decoration.
"Curvature tensor κ(t)" on a 1-D odds series is 3-D language for
`|y''|/(1+y'²)^{3/2}`.

Steam kill line, if anyone logs it: vs a named dumb baseline of
absolute implied-probability delta per unit time, predict closing-line
**direction** on 200+ archived movements, fixture-grouped. No improvement
→ keep the baseline, do not graduate curvature.

### 5. Latency arbitrage is a product we are not in. Kill.

200–400 ms is a **biomechanical** hip-flip number, borrowed, not measured
on bookmaker APIs. Our missed edge is a six-hourly cron, not a stale
secondary book. "Risk-free closing line value" is a claim that needs a
fill, a latency, and a legal venue. We have none of those. Agree with
opus: kill the section. Do not analogize ESOE into an execution strategy.

### 6. Barber citation. Retracting my 10Hz wording.

I previously wrote "Barber et al. 2020 binary-probability bounded-length
impossibility: real, correctly invoked." The **claim** is real. The
**citation** points at the wrong paper. Opus is right; I checked the
primaries.

- Cited (implicitly): Barber, Candès, Ramdas, Tibshirani, "The limits of
  distribution-free conditional predictive inference," *Information and
  Inference* 10(2):455–482. General conditional inference.
- Needed: Rina Foygel Barber (**solo**), "Is distribution-free inference
  possible for binary regression?", *Electronic Journal of Statistics*
  14(2):3487–3524, 2020. arXiv:2004.09477. This is the binary result:
  any distribution-free CI for π(X)=P(Y=1|X) has length bounded below
  independently of n, for nonatomic distributions.

Nothing we concluded changes. A public methodology page that says
"Barber et al. 2020" sends the reader to the four-author paper. Cite
Barber, EJS 2020.

### 7. Valuation integral is expected points. Widened Gaussian is the baseline, not the product.

V = ∫ g_EP(y) f(y|s) dy is E[points | state]. Logging N(point,
historical residual σ) as "full margin densities" in Rung 1 creates a
dataset whose CRPS later "evaluates" a decoration of the point estimate.
Same mean, fixed σ: the density adds no information. Honest Rung 1: log
the point, log the frozen prior-season σ, label it **baseline**. A density
model has to change the shape (mixture, skew, discrete support on 3 and 7)
or it is a point model scored with CRPS.

"Knightian uncertainty" is unmeasurable uncertainty (Knight 1921).
Conformal coverage is a frequentist probability. The paper uses the word
and then computes α. Vocabulary.

### 8. Δp > 0.20 is unmeasured, and our IVAP empty-set would auto-pass it.

Venn-Abers width is a function of calibration n and score overlap. I did
not run it on production rows (no DB in this sandbox). The threshold is
therefore a guess of the same type as 5%. Worse: `InductiveVennAbers`
with empty calibration returns width 0. A Δp>0.20 gate on that file as
written would **issue** the bet in the one case it must refuse.

Kill line before the gate ships: log width as-of on the shadow path
(files exist). If at n_cal ≥ 50 the median width is never < 0.20, the
threshold never fires and is decoration. If empty-cal width is 0, the
gate is inverted. Fix the file first (`width: 1` or throw, not 0).

---

## D. What I would NOT build. A review that rejects nothing is not a review.

1. **Shin as the receipt de-vig.** Paper's direction is backwards, our tests
   already have the correct one, basis change resets PROVEN, causal story
   disputed (Whelan 2025). Founder-only if ever.
2. **Gaussian CRPS as the primary score**, and the 0.01 / n=150 gate as
   written (both directions). Implement discrete CRPS. Kill line in C.1.
3. **Jackknife+ on n=70 H2H.** Sample destruction. ±18 pt intervals.
   Do not stack ACI on it and print 1−2α.
4. **"Build Venn-Abers" / "strip CQR clamp" / "add ACI" as new work.**
   Files exist. Remaining work is fail-closing the copies that still clamp
   or return width 0, and wiring, not rewriting PAVA.
5. **RTS-smoothed B-spline steam as a live capital gate.** Lookahead, not
   parameter-free, no kill vs simple delta. Hawkes was already the right
   shape of "do not fit this on three weeks of data."
6. **Latency arbitrage / 200–400 ms stale-book execution.** Not our product.
7. **Tracking pipeline, Triton, Arrow Flight, 13 m/s gates.** Conceded, still
   rights-blocked, irrelevant without a feed.
8. **Encoding 5% / 19% / Δp=0.20 / CRPS<0.01 as constants.** None measured
   on our data.
9. **Replacing Brier for binary sides.**

---

## E. What I would build, from the learning-loop seat, in order.

These are not the paper's rungs. They are the paper minus the inverted
gates, minus the rebuilds, minus the sample destruction.

1. **Wire `readTrainableTrueProb` at every trainer / ranking read.** Report
   the refusal count. Fail-close `ranking-prob.ts` (untagged ≡ refuse, not
   "not backfill"). This is the charter hole the paper does not know about
   and it outranks every density idea. Opus flagged it; it is still open.

2. **Fail-close the remaining conformal copies in `packages/**`.**
   `conformal-intervals.ts` quantile clamp → +Infinity, matching `cqr.ts`.
   `cqrInterval` empty-cal currently returns `qhat: 0` and the raw
   unexpanded interval (`cqr.ts:40-42`). `ivap.ts` empty-cal width 0.
   Three holes, same polarity, my domain.

3. **Implement `crpsDiscrete` (kernel contract already written).** Log it
   as-of against the widened Gaussian **baseline** (prior-season σ, frozen).
   Rung 1 log, rung 2 on n≥272 game-level margins, kill in C.1. No market
   term. Do not wait for a neural density.

4. **Log Venn-Abers `[p0,p1]` as-of on the shadow path** (files exist).
   Measure median Δp before any 0.20 gate. Fix empty-cal first.

5. **Climatology kill line: frozen prior-season home-win constant**, not
   0.5. Opus is right and I will take that on the climatology file after
   this. A constant 0.57 beats 0.5 with zero skill; we have already been
   burned by a Brier floor a base-rate forecast clears.

---

## F. Charter ladder.

| Component | Rung | Named dumb baseline | Pre-registered kill |
|---|---|---|---|
| trueProb trainer gate | 0 (leakage) | — | any fit on untagged / post_settlement_backfill is a defect, not a result |
| Market-clock plausibility | 1 | — | log violation rate; do not encode 5% |
| Widened Gaussian density | 1 (baseline, labelled) | historical residual σ, prior seasons only | — |
| Discrete CRPS vs that Gaussian | 2 | Gaussian CRPS with frozen prior-season σ, no market | CRPS not better by 0.5 at n≥272 game margins, fixture-grouped → keep the Gaussian |
| Venn-Abers width (existing files) | 1 log, 2 later | — | empty-cal width 0 is a defect; median Δp never <0.20 at n_cal≥50 → threshold is decoration |
| Jackknife+ | 2 only on large n | split CQR on the SAME large sample | width at 80% > 14 pts on holdout → coverage trophy, do not bet |
| ACI | 2 vs static split, not stacked on Jackknife+ | static split coverage error | coverage error not lower → keep static |
| Shin vs proportional | 3 research only | proportional (current receipt) | founder-only to switch; streak reset is the cost |
| E-process | 3, our ratio not the paper's | market likelihood | implement from `forecast-skill-eprocess.ts`, never from the paper |
| B-spline steam | 1 log if at all | abs Δp / Δt | no CL-direction skill on 200+ moves → drop |
| Latency arb | cannot map | — | kill |
| Tracking / 13 m/s | cannot map | — | blocked on rights |

A rung-2 survivor is real and enters the engine whether or not it ever
beats a line. Nothing in this paper that costs the PROVEN streak, fits on
the future line, or ships a gate whose number cannot fire, is rung 2.

---

## What I did not verify, stated plainly

- The 5% market-violation rate. Not measured. I will not invent it.
- VERSA 19%. No primary opened. Still uncited.
- Empirical NFL margin σ on **our** settled rows. I used 14 as a literature
  ballpark. If our σ is 10, E[CRPS]≈5.6 and 0.01 is still 0.03 SE at n=150.
  The power conclusion is robust to that.
- Production Venn-Abers widths. No DB here. That is why Δp>0.20 stays a guess.
- Shin 1993 quadratic against the JSTOR PDF. I used the standard Cain/Clarke
  implementation that our `shinDevig` also uses. Direction does not depend
  on the year (1992 vs 1993) of the header.
- Yurko et al. 2020 "Going Deep" against the PDF this round (verified as real
  in the 10Hz pass).
- Lin/Trivedi/Sun 2021: still the Bai et al. 2021 misattribution from the
  first paper; this blueprint does not repeat the formula.

---

## One-sentence verdict

The paper correctly drops tracking, then spends the pages it freed on inverted
gates (CRPS, Shin, first-paper E-process), unmeasurable constants, and a
rebuild list of files we already have; the learning-loop work is fail-closing
the copies that still clamp, wiring the trueProb gate, and scoring integer
margins with discrete CRPS against a frozen Gaussian baseline — none of which
the paper specified in a form we can ship.
